basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 2.' and it opens '(Cap. XLI.—Vers. 2.) Et ecce de fluvio ascendebant septem boves, speciosae ad videndum,'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Cap. XLI.—Vers. 2.) Et ecce de fluvio ascendebant septem boves, speciosae ad videndum, electae carnibus, et pascebantur in achi. Bis in Genesi scriptum est ACHI (Ἄχα), et neque Graecus sermo est, nec Latinus. Sed et Hebraeus ipse corruptus est: dicitur enim in AHU (אחו), hoc est, in palude. Sed quia VAU littera apud Hebraeos, et IOD similes sunt, et tantum magnitudine differunt: pro AHU, ACHI Septuaginta Interpretes transtulerunt, et secundum consuetudinem suam ad exprimendam duplicem aspirationem, HETH Hebraeae litterae, Chi (χ) Graecam litteram copulaverunt.
